PHILADELPHIA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Datavault AI Inc. (“Datavault” or the “Company”) (OTC: DVLT), today announced that the Company expects its common stock will be eligible to trade on the over-the-counter market (“OTC Markets”) effective with the open of the market on November 17, 2026. The move to OTC Markets follows Nasdaq’s decision to suspend trading in the Company’s common stock effective November 17, 2026, due to the Company’s non-compliance with Nasdaq’s $1.00 minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) and the “low stock price” rule set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iii), which requires a suspension of Nasdaq trading for an issuer that evidences a closing bid price of less than $0.10 per share for ten consecutive business days.

The Company intends to request a hearing before the Nasdaq Hearings Panel to maintain its Nasdaq listing. At the hearing, the Company will present its plan to evidence compliance with the bid price requirement and to request an extension of time to do so and the reinitiation of trading and continued listing of the Company’s securities on Nasdaq as a result thereof.

About Datavault AI

Datavault AI Inc. verifies, values and tokenizes data and real-world assets for organizations and people. Its exchanges bring those assets to market. Through its media, acoustic and live-event technologies and services, the Company powers how organizations reach and engage customers across business and consumer channels. Its technologies are protected by a portfolio of issued patents, which the Company makes available through licensing. Learn more at www.dvlt.ai.

The first of many planned destinations is drawing a new generation of fans

NASHVILLE, Tenn.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Travel + Leisure Co. (NYSE:TNL), a leading leisure travel and hospitality company, officially opens Sports Illustrated Resorts Nashville today, launching a national hospitality brand built around the games, teams and events fans love. The 185-suite resort on Music Row, one mile from downtown Nashville and the Gulch, is the first of four announced destinations totaling more than 800 suites and units.

Travel + Leisure Co., a leading leisure travel and hospitality company, officially opens Sports Illustrated Resorts Nashville today, launching a national hospitality brand built around the games, teams and events fans love. The 185-suite resort on Music Row, one mile from downtown Nashville and the Gulch, is the first of four announced destinations totaling more than 800 suites and units.

Sports Illustrated Resorts launched with its vacation club and is expanding into hotels and condominium residences — with each destination offering its own mix of stays shaped by its city and the fans it draws. Chicago’s full brand offering is expected in spring 2027, followed by a phased opening in Baton Rouge later in 2027 and the brand’s first ground-up resort in Tuscaloosa in 2028. Baton Rouge will be the first property to combine the vacation club, a hotel and condominium residences.

Since its soft opening in September, Sports Illustrated Resorts Nashville has seen Titans and Vanderbilt home-game weekends rank among its busiest, and 95% of guests surveyed after their stay gave top marks to the resort’s signature suite design.

The resort’s first vacation club owners, known as MVPs, represent an all-new base of owners within the Travel + Leisure Co. portfolio and span two generations of fans. More than half are 45 or younger, including one in three between the ages of 26 and 35. Another 36% are 46 to 65, prime years for parents traveling to college campuses for game days, family weekends and move-ins. And the brand’s draw is national: nearly four in five owners live outside Tennessee. College sports travel is a major opportunity for the brand: in a 2025 Travel + Leisure Co. survey of sports travelers, 87% had traveled for a college sporting event in the past three years.

A New Way to Travel for the Game

“Opening Sports Illustrated Resorts Nashville is a milestone for the brand, and the early response tells us we’re onto something,” said Geoff Richards, chief operating officer at Travel + Leisure Co. “Sports are one of the biggest reasons people travel, and fans want a vacation built around that passion. We’re seeing it in who’s buying: a new, younger generation of fans, alongside parents who plan their fall around their kids’ college campuses. Sports bring them all to the same place. Nashville is where it starts, and every resort we open next will take the experience further.”

Travel + Leisure Co. operates Sports Illustrated Resorts under a license from Authentic Brands Group, owner of the Sports Illustrated brand.

“For more than 70 years, Sports Illustrated has brought fans closer to the moments that define the games they love,” said Daniel W. Dienst, Executive Vice Chairman, Tactical Opportunities at Authentic Brands Group. “We’re so proud to watch our partners at Travel + Leisure Co. kick off the roll out of Sports Illustrated Resorts in Nashville and even more excited to watch them execute this unique concept in many other sports destinations across the U.S.”

Athletes on the Roster

Athletes are a core part of the Sports Illustrated Resorts experience, from signature suites to appearances at resort events like tonight’s opening celebration in Nashville. Seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion and owner of LEGACY MOTOR CLUB, Jimmie Johnson, has joined Sports Illustrated Resorts as a brand ambassador. Through the partnership, Johnson will appear at Sports Illustrated Resorts openings, owner events and marquee sports experiences, and create content with the brand.

“I’ve spent my whole career traveling to race weekends, and the best trips were always the ones where family and friends could come along and be part of it,” said Johnson. “Sports Illustrated Resorts is built for exactly that: a home base where fans can share the game, the trip and the time together. I’m proud to be part of it from day one.”

Johnson joins Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis, who partnered with Sports Illustrated Resorts on the Jared Curtis Suite, a one-of-a-kind suite at the Nashville resort inspired by his journey on and off the field. The suite is now available to book.

Where Sports and Vacation Come Together

Sports Illustrated Resorts Nashville offers 185 studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom suites, each with a full kitchen and in-unit laundry, perfect for gameday trips, college visits or weekend getaways.

Signature amenities are designed to bring fans together before, during and after the game:

  • A fitness center, SI Fit, inspired by the training and performance mindset of elite athletes
  • A sports bar for watching games and gathering with fellow fans
  • A game room with interactive entertainment for guests of all ages
  • A tailgate deck for gameday celebrations and events
  • A Sports Concierge to connect guests with local games, sporting events and destination experiences
  • A through line of Sports Illustrated design and content woven throughout the resort

MVP benefits include a VIP Ticket Concierge, an annual experience credit toward concerts, sporting events and festivals, exclusive event drops released throughout the year, and a one-year Sports Illustrated magazine subscription. Through Varsity Pass, owners can book stays at 45 destinations across the country, with more than 3,600 additional resorts worldwide available through RCI Exchange.

Sports Illustrated Resorts Nashville is open to all travelers for nightly and weekend stays, with vacation club owners receiving priority access to suites and dates. To book a stay or learn more, visit www.sportsillustratedresorts.com and follow Sports Illustrated Resorts on Instagram @SIResorts.

About Sports Illustrated Resorts

Where champions come to stay. Inspired by the most iconic name in sports and designed for the fans who live for it, Sports Illustrated Resorts is a new hospitality brand where the season never ends. From college towns alive with tradition to cities charged with culture and competition, every destination blends the Sports Illustrated legacy with distinctive stays, premium experiences and the unmistakable thrill of game day, across its vacation club, hotels and condominium residences. Signature spaces like SI Fit, partnerships with athletes and exclusive access to marquee sporting events bring fans closer to the game than ever. Sports Illustrated Resorts is operated by Travel + Leisure Co. under a license from Authentic Brands Group, with a growing portfolio of destinations across the U.S. Learn more at sportsillustratedresorts.com and follow @SIResorts on Instagram.

About Travel + Leisure Co.

Travel + Leisure Co. (NYSE:TNL) is a leading leisure travel company, providing more than six million vacations to travelers around the world every year. The company operates a portfolio of vacation ownership, travel club, and lifestyle travel brands designed to meet the needs of the modern leisure traveler, whether they’re traversing the globe or staying a little closer to home. With hospitality and responsible tourism at its heart, the company’s nearly 19,000 dedicated associates around the globe help the company achieve its mission to put the world on vacation. Learn more at travelandleisureco.com.

About Sports Illustrated

For over 70 years, Sports Illustrated (SI) has been recognized for shaping modern culture at the intersection of sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. SI is a 360-degree platform that unites athletes, teams and fans worldwide through quality content, innovative digital experiences, unforgettable events, and original products. Its award-winning media arm brings powerful storytelling to life through probing profiles and up-to-date news on SI.com, across social media platforms, and through its renowned print magazine whose cover is widely regarded as the most coveted space in sports media. The most trusted name in sports transcends media through SI Tickets, a fan-first ticketing platform, SI Resorts, the ultimate destination for active lifestyles & sports enthusiasts, SI Studios, the brand’s home for film, TV, and long form podcasts, and more. SI brings its unique perspective to marquee events and captivating brand activations including “SI The Party”, Club SI, the Sportsperson of the Year Awards, SI Swimsuit Launch Weekend, and the SI Circuit Series.

For more information, visit SI.com.

Follow Sports Illustrated on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Calidi Biotherapeutics, Inc. (NYSE American: CLDI) ("Calidi" or the "Company"), a biotechnology company pioneering the development of targeted genetic medicines, today reported financial and operating results for the three months ended September 30, 2026, and reviewed recent business highlights.

“Throughout the third quarter, Calidi continued to advance its RedTail platform for systemic and local delivery and redefine the potential of oncolytic viruses and genetic medicine,” said Eric Poma, Ph.D., Calidi Biotherapeutics CEO. “In particular, CLD-401 demonstrated remarkable anti-tumor activity with systemic administration in syngeneic tumor models and continues to progress towards the clinic.”

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Developments

  • Presented two posters at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 on October 24, 2026. The presentations showcased new data from the Company’s RedTail platform, a systemically delivered virotherapy platform engineered to selectively target tumors, remodel the tumor microenvironment, and enable high-level expression of therapeutic genetic payloads directly within tumors.
    • Preclinical data on Calidi’s lead program, CLD-401, showed complete tumor eradication in 80% of EMT6 breast cancer tumor-bearing mice versus 0% in the control arm. CLD-401 was engineered for systemic delivery, and new data from an MB49 bladder cancer model show it retains antitumor activity with either systemic intravenous or localized intratumoral administration, supporting flexible delivery approaches across tumor accessibility and disease settings. 
    • Presented preclinical data from Calidi’s in situ T-cell engager (“TCE”) platform, including CLD-501, its TROP-2-targeted candidate, and CLD-502, its EpCAM-targeted candidate.   Following intravenous delivery, the platform generated approximately 10 ng/mL of EpCAM-targeted TCE directly within tumors, and both targeted TCEs demonstrated antigen-dependent, does-responsive T-cell mediated cytotoxicity.
  • Received $1.2 million gross proceeds from an at-the-market registered direct offering that closed on September 18, 2026.
  • Reduced general and administrative expenses by $1.0 million, or 39%, in the third quarter of 2026 versus the same period in the prior year. Reduced general and administrative expenses by $3.6 million, or 42%, in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, versus the same period in the prior year. On November 6, 2026, Calidi executed a restructuring plan, predominantly through a reduction in headcount, that is expected to save $3 million on an annualized basis to extend the Company’s cash runway to reduce costs, extend the Company's operating runway, and preserve capital while pursuing additional financing. 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Calidi reported a $3.6 million net loss attributable to common stockholders for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $10.8 million for the third quarter of 2025, which included a $5.7 million non-cash charge for a deemed dividend on warrants.  There was no such charge during the third quarter of 2026.

Research and development expenses were $2.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $2.4 million for the same quarter in 2025.

General and administrative expenses were $1.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $2.7 million for the same quarter in 2025.

The Company had $3.9 million in cash and $0.2 million in restricted cash as of September 30, 2026, compared with $5.6 million in cash and $0.2 million in restricted cash as of December 31. 2025.

About Calidi Biotherapeutics

Calidi Biotherapeutics (NYSE American: CLDI) is a biotechnology company pioneering the development of targeted therapies with the potential to deliver genetic medicines to distal sites of disease. The Company’s proprietary RedTail platform features an engineered enveloped oncolytic virus designed for systemic delivery and targeting of metastatic sites. This advanced enveloped technology is intended to shield the virus from immune clearance, allowing virotherapy to effectively reach tumor sites, induce tumor lysis, and deliver potent genetic medicine(s) to metastatic locations.

CLD-401, the lead candidate from the RedTail platform, currently in IND-enabling studies, targets metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, head and neck cancer, and other tumor types with high unmet medical need. Calidi continues to advance its pipeline utilizing the RedTail platform including its novel approach to incorporate in situ T-cell engagers in solid tumors.

Calidi Biotherapeutics is headquartered in San Diego, California. For more information, please visit www.calidibio.com.

IRVINE, Calif., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cheetah Net Supply Chain Service Inc. (“Cheetah” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq CM: CTNT), a provider of logistics and warehousing services and international trading services, today reported results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided a corporate update.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported total revenue of $3,557,805, compared to $361,935 in the same period in 2025, representing an increase of $3,195,870, or 883.0%. The Company recorded an operating loss of $821,890 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, compared to an operating loss of $1,564,479 in the same period in 2025, representing a decrease of $742,589, or 47.5%. The decrease was primarily due to an increase of $237,229 in gross profit and the absence of an impairment loss of $731,307 recognized in the same period in 2025, partially offset by an increase of $287,851 in general and administrative expenses compared to the same period in 2025. The Company recognized other expenses, net, of $1,726,105 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, primarily attributable to a $2,783,884 loss resulting from the change in fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration asset, partially offset by interest income of $398,232 and other income of $666,508. After accounting for an income tax provision of nil, the Company reported a net loss from continuing operations of $2,547,995, compared to net loss from continuing operations of $1,314,650 for the same period in 2025, representing an increase in net loss of $1,233,345, or 93.8%.

Tony Liu, Cheetah’s Chairman and CEO, commented: “The third quarter of 2026 marked an important step forward in the execution of our business diversification strategy. Following the acquisition of Super International Trading Limited in May, our international trading business demonstrated encouraging momentum, generating approximately $3.56 million in revenue during the quarter. This performance reflects the progress we have made in expanding our business platform and developing new sources of revenue.”

“While our logistics and warehousing business continues to face challenges arising from evolving global trade conditions and cross-border customer demand, we remain focused on optimizing our operating structure and allocating resources toward opportunities that we believe offer greater long-term growth potential. We are encouraged by the progress of our international trading business and will continue to focus on strengthening its operations, expanding business opportunities, and improving operational efficiency.”

“Looking ahead, we remain committed to disciplined capital allocation, prudent financial management, and the pursuit of strategic opportunities that complement our existing capabilities. We believe that our continued efforts to diversify our revenue streams and strengthen our operating platform will position the Company for sustainable long-term growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Continuing operations – logistics and warehousing business

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $nil from its logistics and warehousing services segment, compared to $361,935 for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the disposition of Edward and the expiration of TWEW’s legacy customer service contracts during late 2025 and early 2026, which were not renewed on their original terms. As of the date of this release, TWEW is renegotiating logistics and labor services arrangements with customers that had business relationships with TWEW prior to its acquisition, and letters of intent and draft contracts with certain of these customers are in the process of being executed.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $nil and $317,757 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a decrease of $317,757, or 100.0%, consistent with the corresponding decline in revenue from Edward and TWEW.

Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $nil, a decrease of $44,178, or 100.0%, from $44,178 for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations-logistics and warehousing services segment decreased by $90,368, or 84.1%, to $17,068 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $107,436 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the disposal of Edward in 2026.

Continuing operations – international trading

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $3,557,805 from its international trading segment, all of which was generated by Super International Trading Limited (“Super International”), which we acquired on May 27, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the expansion of the Company’s international trading business following the acquisition of Super International.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $3,276,398 and $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing an increase of $3,276,398, all of which was attributable to Super International, consistent with the corresponding increase in international trading revenue.

Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $281,407, an increase of $281,407, from $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations - international trading segment increased to $23,349 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to the commencement of the Company’s international trading operations following the acquisition of Super International on May 27, 2026.

Continuing operations – Corporate Unallocated Operating Adjustments

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations- corporate unallocated operating adjustments segment increased by $354,870, or 51.1%, to $1,048,697 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $693,827 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to travel and entertainment expenses and legal and accounting fees and other general and administrative expenses.

Share-based compensation expenses were $14,183 and $76,087 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a decrease of $61,904, or 81.4%.

Interest income from continuing operations was $398,232 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $244,776 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $153,456 or 62.7%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in average outstanding loan balances as the Company made additional loans to third parties, resulting in higher interest income.

Interest expense incurred from our continuing operations was $6,961 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which decreased by $888, or 11.3%, from $7,849 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, mainly due to the continued amortization of our long-term borrowings and lower credit card and premium finance interest.

Net other income from continuing operations was $666,508 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $12,902 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $653,606, or 5,065.9%. The increase was primarily driven by higher foreign exchange gains resulting from currency rate fluctuations.

The Company’s receivable from withdrawal of investment deposit of $41,762,995 as of September 30, 2026, represents RMB 280,000,000 contributed by Naiside to a PRC investment fund in January 2026 and repayable in full by Shanghai Kesheng on or before December 30, 2026. The receivable is denominated in Renminbi and remeasured at each reporting date. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized an unrealized foreign exchange gain of $652,422 on this receivable. Excluding this non-cash gain, the Company’s loss from continuing operations before income taxes of $2,547,995 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 would have been approximately $3,200,417.

Other expense from the change in fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration asset was $2,783,884 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

As a result of the above factors, the Company had a net loss of $2,547,995 from continuing operations for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $1,314,650 for the same period of 2025.

Nine Months 2026 Financial Results

Continuing operations – logistics and warehousing business

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $92,700 from its logistics and warehousing services segment, compared to $1,195,860 for the same period in 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the disposition of Edward and the expiration of TWEW’s legacy customer service contracts, as described above.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $72,833 and $1,060,526 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, primarily reflecting labor and logistics costs for TWEW and ocean freight service costs incurred by Edward.

Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $19,867, a decrease of $115,467, or 85.3%, from $135,334 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations-logistics and warehousing services segment decreased by $179,749, or 50.8%, to $173,757 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $353,506 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was mainly due to lower operating and administrative expenses following the disposal of Edward, as well as ongoing cost control initiatives.

Continuing operations – international trading

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company reported revenue of $4,426,714 from its international trading segment, of which $208,909, or 4.7%, was attributable to Cheetah, and $4,217,805, or 95.3%, was attributable to Super International, which the Company acquired on May 27, 2026. The increase was primarily due to the expansion of the Company’s international trading business following the acquisition of Super International.

The Company also reported cost of revenue of $4,125,807 and $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing an increase of $4,125,807 including $199,409 attributable to Cheetah and $3,926,398 attributable to Super International, consistent with the corresponding increase in international trading revenue.

Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, was $300,907, an increase of $300,907, from $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations-international trading segment increased to $43,433 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to the acquisition of Super International.

Continuing operations – Corporate Unallocated Operating Adjustments

General and administrative expenses for the Company’s continuing operations- corporate unallocated operating adjustments segment increased by $275,462, or 12.2%, to $2,529,043 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from $2,253,581 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was mainly due to an increase in travel and entertainment expenses and other general and administrative expenses.

Share-based compensation expenses were $42,547 and $102,716 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, representing a decrease of $60,169, or 58.6%.

Interest income from continuing operations was $814,069 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $725,094 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $88,975 or 12.3%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in average outstanding loan balances as the Company made additional loans to third parties, resulting in higher interest income.

Interest expense incurred from our continuing operations was $21,460 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which decreased by $3,261, or 13.2%, from $24,721 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, mainly due to lower average outstanding balances under long-term borrowings and premium finance arrangements.

Net other income from continuing operations was $1,669,286 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $42,658 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase of $1,626,628, or 3,813.2%. The increase was primarily driven by higher foreign exchange gains resulting from currency rate fluctuations.

During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recognized an unrealized foreign exchange gain of approximately $1,631,708 related to the receivable arising from the withdrawal of the investment deposit. Excluding this non-cash gain, the Company would have incurred a loss from continuing operations before income taxes of approximately $4,719,313 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Other expense from the change in fair value of acquisition-related contingent consideration asset was $2,783,884 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

As a result of the above factors, the Company had a net loss of $3,093,215 from continuing operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a net loss of $2,581,087 for the same period of 2025.

Liquidity and Going Concern Considerations

The Company reported a net loss of approximately $3.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and net cash used in operating activities of approximately $2.5 million. As the Company continues to integrate its newly acquired international trading business and develop its logistics and warehousing service business, the Company may continue to incur operating losses and generate negative cash flow. These factors were considered in management’s evaluation of the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern, together with the mitigating factors described below.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $14.5 million and a working capital balance of $87.1 million. In addition, the Company had a receivable from withdrawal of investment deposit of $41.8 million and loans receivable from third parties of approximately $29.5 million, which can be sufficient for the Company to support its ongoing business operations and meet the obligations in the future.

Management has evaluated the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern in accordance with ASC 205-40, Presentation of Financial Statements – Going Concern. This evaluation considered the Company’s current financial condition, expected cash flows, obligations due within the next 12 months, and available sources of liquidity.

The Company is working to further improve its liquidity and capital sources primarily by generating cash from operations, pursuing debt financing, and, if needed, seeking financial support from its principal stockholder. If necessary to fully implement its business plan and sustain continued growth, the Company may seek additional equity financing from outside investors. Based on the current operating plan, management believes that the aforementioned measures collectively will provide sufficient liquidity to meet the Company’s liquidity and capital requirements for at least 12 months from the issuance date of its consolidated financial statements.

NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly-E Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: FLYE) ("Fly-E" or the "Company"), an electric vehicle company engaged in designing, installing, selling, and renting smart electric motorcycles, electric bikes, and electric scooters, today announced its unaudited financial results for the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2027 ended September 30, 2026.

Second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Summary

  • Net revenues were $2.6 million, compared to $3.9 million in the same period last year.
  • Gross profit was $0.2 million, compared to $1.0 million in the same period last year.
  • Gross margin was 8.1%, compared to 25.0% in the same period last year.
  • Net Loss was $1.7 million, compared to $1.8 million in the same period last year.
  • Basic and diluted losses per share were $1.07, compared to $2.18 in the same period last year.

Mr. Zhou (Andy) Ou, Chief Executive Officer of Fly-E, commented, "During the second quarter, our operational network stabilized following the retail restructuring, with our top-line revenue holding steady sequentially. Our wholesale revenues grew 21.4% year-over-year and accounted for a significantly higher proportion of our total revenue. This evolving revenue mix, combined with promotional pricing in our retail business, naturally influenced our overall margin profile for the period. Meanwhile, we continued to control store-level costs and address corporate matters carefully to strengthen the Company's foundation for the future. By maintaining our operational network and disciplined cost management, we are dedicated to preserving business stability while positioning Fly-E to explore strategic opportunities for long-term growth."

Second quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

(Three Months Ended September 30, 2026)

Net Revenues

Net revenues were $2.6 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 33.7% from $3.9 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily driven by a lower sales volume of 7,392 units in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to 18,564 in the same period last year, resulting from the reduction in our direct retail store count to four stores as of September 30, 2026, compared to 11 stores as of September 30, 2025.

  • Retail sales revenue was $0.5 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 77.4% from $2.0 million in the same period last year. The decline was primarily driven by planned store reductions, promotional pricing strategies in response to market competition, and softened consumer demand for E-Bikes and E-Scooters following industry-wide lithium-ion battery safety concerns in the New York market.
  • Wholesale revenue was $2.1 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, an increase of 21.4% from $1.7 million in the same period last year. This growth was primarily due to ongoing product purchases from previous company-owned retail stores that transitioned to independent operations during the period.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues was $2.4 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 18.8% from $2.9 million in the same period last year, primarily aligning with lower sales volume driven by the downsizing of our retail store network.

Gross Profit and Margin

Gross profit was $0.2 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to $1.0 million in the same period last year. Gross margin was 8.1% in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to 25.0% in the same period last year. The decrease in gross margin was primarily attributable to a structural mix shift from direct retail toward lower-priced wholesale channels, further impacted by competitive retail pricing and inventory clearance discounts.

Total Operating Expenses

Total operating expenses were $1.8 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 9.8% compared to $2.0 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily attributable to store-level operational savings, which were partially offset by increases in expected credit losses and professional fees.

  • Selling expenses were $0.3 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a significant decrease of 74.3% from $1.0 million in the same period last year, primarily driven by the reduction of retail stores which significantly lowered associated payroll, rental and utility expenses.
  • General and administrative expenses were $1.5 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, an increase of 56.6% from $1.0 million in the same period last year. The increase was primarily attributable to expected credit losses on prepayments and receivables and litigation-related legal fees, which were partially offset by cost savings in payroll and software development expenses.

Net Loss

Net loss was $1.7 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to $1.8 million in the same period last year.

Basic and Diluted Earnings (Losses) per Share

Basic and diluted losses per share were $1.07 in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to $2.18 in the same period last year.

EBITDA

EBITDA was negative $1.3 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, compared to negative EBITDA of $1.0 million in the same period last year.

First Half of Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

(Six Months Ended September 30, 2026)

Net Revenues

Net revenues were $5.3 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 42.2% from $9.2 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily driven by a significant reduction in direct retail store counts, resulting in a lower sales volume of 14,950 units in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to 29,012 in the same period last year.

  • Retail sales revenue was $1.0 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 81.9% from $5.8 million in the same period last year. The decline was primarily due to significant retail store downsizing, promotional pricing adjustments, and lithium-ion battery safety headwinds in the New York market.
  • Wholesale revenue was $4.2 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, an increase of 33.0% from $3.2 million in the same period last year. This increase was primarily attributable to ongoing product purchases from the retail stores that were streamlined and transitioned to independent operations during the period.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues was $4.8 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 19.5% from $6.0 million in the same period last year, primarily reflecting lower sales volume following the downsizing of our retail store network.

Gross Profit and Margin

Gross profit was $0.5 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to $3.2 million in the same period last year. Gross margin was 9.5% in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to 35.1% in the same period last year. The decrease in gross margin was primarily attributable to the greater revenue percentage of wholesale channels at lower-priced wholesale pricing, as well as promotional retail pricing adjustment and inventory clearance discounts.

Total Operating Expenses

Total operating expenses were $5.7 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a decrease of 2.2% compared to $5.8 million in the same period last year. The decrease was primarily attributable to operational cost savings from retail store reductions, which were offset by increases in expected credit losses and software development fees.

  • Selling expenses were $0.8 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, a significant decrease of 68.1% from $2.3 million in the same period last year, primarily driven by the reductions in store-level payroll and rental expenses following retail store network downsizing.
  • General and administrative expenses were $4.8 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, an increase of 42.7% from $3.4 million in the same period last year. The increase was primarily attributable to expected credit losses on prepayments and receivables and software development fees for our ERP and mobile applications, which were partially offset by decreases in professional fees, payroll and insurance expenses.

Net Loss

Net loss was $5.6 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to $3.8 million in the same period last year.

Basic and Diluted Earnings (Losses) per Share

Basic and diluted losses per share were $3.48 in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to $6.58 in the same period last year.

EBITDA

EBITDA was negative $4.7 million in the first half of fiscal year 2027, compared to negative EBITDA of $2.2 million in the same period last year.

Financial Condition

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash of $0.5 million, compared to $0.3 million as of March 31, 2026.

About Fly-E Group, Inc.

Fly-E Group, Inc. is an electric vehicle company that is principally engaged in designing, installing, selling, and renting smart electric motorcycles, electric bikes, and electric scooters under the brand "Fly E-Bike." The Company's commitment is to encourage people to incorporate eco-friendly transportation into their active lifestyles, ultimately contributing towards building a more environmentally friendly future. For more information, please visit the Company's website: https://investors.flyebike.com.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

To supplement our financial information presented in accordance with the generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (the "U.S. GAAP"), management periodically uses certain "non-GAAP financial measures," as such term is defined under the rules of the SEC, to clarify and enhance understanding of past performance and prospects for the future. Generally, a non-GAAP financial measure is a numerical measure of a company's operating performance, financial position or cash flows that excludes or includes amounts that are included in or excluded from the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. For example, non-GAAP measures may exclude the impact of certain items such as acquisitions, divestitures, gains, losses and impairments, or items outside of management's control. Management believes that the following non-GAAP financial measure provides investors and analysts useful insight into our financial position and operating performance. Any non-GAAP measure provided should be viewed in addition to, and not as an alternative to, the most directly comparable measure determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Further, the calculation of these non-GAAP financial measures may differ from the calculation of similarly titled financial measures presented by other companies and therefore may not be comparable among companies.

We use EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization) to evaluate our operating performance. We believe EBITDA provides additional insight into our underlying, ongoing operating performance and facilitates year-to-year comparisons by excluding the earnings impact of interest, tax, depreciation and amortization and that presenting EBITDA is more representative of our operational performance and may be more useful for investors.

We reconcile our non-GAAP financial measure to our net income, which is our most directly comparable financial measure calculated and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. EBITDA includes adjustments for provision for income taxes, as applicable, interest income and expense, depreciation, and amortization. EBITDA does not represent and should not be considered an alternative to net income as determined by U.S. GAAP, and our calculations thereof may not be comparable to those reported by other companies. We believe EBITDA is an important measure of operating performance and provides useful information to investors because it highlights trends in our business that may not otherwise be apparent when relying solely on U.S. GAAP measures and because it eliminates items that have less bearing on our operating performance. EBITDA, as presented herein, is a supplemental measure of our performance that is not required by, or presented in accordance with, U.S. GAAP. We use non-GAAP financial measures as supplements to our U.S. GAAP results in order to provide a more complete understanding of the factors and trends affecting our business. EBITDA is a measure of operating performance that is not defined by U.S. GAAP and should not be considered a substitute for net (loss) income as determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

Vancouver, BC – November 13, 2026 – TheNewswire - Copper One Resources Corp. (“Copper One”) (CSE: CEXY | OTCID: CEXYF | FSE: IW8 | WKN: A42AGR) (the “Company”) announces the completion of drill hole MHB-41, the third hole of its 2026 Phase 2 diamond drilling program of up to 10,000 feet at its 100%-owned flagship Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project (“Majuba Hill” or the “Project”) in Pershing County, Nevada.

MHB-41 reached a final downhole depth of 1,850 feet (564 metres). Preliminary geological core logging identified pervasive silicification with fine-grained pyrite and chalcopyrite, tourmaline breccia at multiple depths, and fracture coatings of hematite and tenorite. These observations provide additional geological information to support the Company’s ongoing evaluation of alteration and mineralization at Majuba Hill.

MHB-41 Highlights

  • Hole orientation and depth: MHB-41 was drilled on a grid azimuth of 075° at an inclination of −50°, reaching a final downhole depth of 1,850 feet (564 metres). 

  • Silicification and sulfides: Core at approximately 580–581 feet pervasive silicification with fine-grained pyrite and chalcopyrite. 

  • Tourmaline breccia: Selected core photographs show tourmaline breccia within core-box intervals of 808.0–817.6 feet and 1,066.7–1,076.3 feet, including angular, pale-coloured clasts within a dark matrix. 

  • Fracture mineralization: Core at 1,261 feet (384 metres) downhole displays fracture coatings of hematite and tenorite. 

  • Phase 2 drilling to date: MHB-39, MHB-40 and MHB-41 account for a combined 4,925 feet (1,501 metres) of completed diamond drilling. 

All depths are downhole. The intervals cited for the tourmaline breccia photographs represent full core-box intervals and do not establish continuous mineralized widths. Mineral identifications are preliminary field observations. Visual observations do not determine metal grades or establish economic mineralization and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

No laboratory assay results from MHB-41 are being reported in this news release. Any material analytical results will be disclosed following receipt, quality assurance/quality control review and evaluation by the Company's Qualified Person.


Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 1: Drilling operations during the completion of hole MHB-41 at Copper One's Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project, Nevada.

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, commented: “Completion of MHB-41 marks another important step in our 2026 Phase 2 drilling program at Majuba Hill. The preliminary geological observations, including silicification, sulfide minerals and tourmaline breccia, provide additional information as our technical team continues to evaluate the project's geological characteristics.

“Majuba Hill remains central to our North American copper exploration strategy. We are focused on systematic drilling, disciplined geological interpretation and advancing our understanding of the mineralized system. Laboratory assays and further technical evaluation will be essential in determining the significance of these observations and guiding future exploration.”


Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 2: Drill core from approximately 1,261 feet (384 metres) downhole in MHB-41, showing fracture coatings of hematite and tenorite. Mineral identifications are based on visual observations and have not been confirmed by laboratory analysis.

The Company’s expanded Phase 2 diamond core drilling program (the “Phase 2 Program”) comprises up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of HQ/PQ diamond core drilling. The Phase 2 Program is intended to accelerate systematic testing of priority targets at Majuba Hill and support the Company’s objective of advancing the Project toward an inaugural mineral resource estimate prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects (“NI 43-101”). More than 95,000 feet (28,956 metres) have been drilled to date at Majuba Hill across more than 100 drill holes.

Phase 2 Program Highlights

  • Expanded program of up to 10,000 feet (3,048 metres) of diamond core drilling. 

  • An initial drilling scope of approximately 5,000 feet (1,524 metres) contracted to Evolve using one portable HQ/PQ core drill. 

  • Continuous, two-shift drilling operations planned 24 hours a day, seven days a week. 

  • Maximum planned hole depth under the initial scope of approximately 1,850 feet (564 metres), with final collar locations, azimuths, inclinations and depths to be determined by the Company’s technical team. 

  • Real-time operational visibility through Evolve’s EVX Connect platform. 


Click Image To View Full Size

Figure 3: Drill core from approximately 580 feet (177 metres) downhole in MHB-41, showing pervasive silicification and fine-grained pyrite and chalcopyrite. Visual observations do not establish copper grades and are not a substitute for laboratory assay results.

Real-Time Drill Program Technology

As previously announced, the Company engaged Evolve Exploration Nevada, LLC (“Evolve”) to undertake the Phase 2 diamond core drilling.

Every Evolve drill rig operates on EVX Connect, Evolve’s real-time operational platform. Through EVX Connect, Copper One expects to receive live drilling metrics, digital Progressive Logs of Drilling (“PLOD”), drill-hole coordinate tracking, streamlined invoicing and high-quality photographs of drill core as it is recovered. Information will be accessible through web and mobile interfaces, providing the Company’s technical and management teams with timely visibility into drilling progress and field operations.

About the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold Project, Nevada

Majuba Hill is Copper One Resources Corp.’s flagship copper-silver-gold exploration project, located in Pershing County, Nevada, USA. Nevada ranked first globally on the Investment Attractiveness Index in the Fraser Institute’s Annual Survey of Mining Companies 2025. The property comprises approximately 9,684 acres (3,919 hectares) and is situated approximately 70 miles (113 road kilometres) southwest of Winnemucca and 156 miles (251 kilometres) northeast of Reno.

The project benefits from excellent infrastructure, including year-round road access, nearby electrical power and water, and access to a skilled mining workforce. Majuba Hill is a past-producing copper mine with an extensive exploration database, including records from historical and recent drilling programs, providing a strong technical foundation for ongoing exploration aimed at further defining the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Exploration has outlined a large copper-silver-gold hydrothermal mineralized system that remains open for expansion. Current exploration is focused on advancing the Company's geological model through systematic drilling, geological mapping, geochemical sampling, and structural interpretation to evaluate the scale, continuity, and significance of mineralization. Additional drilling and technical studies will be required to further define the extent and economic potential of the mineralized system.

Data Verification and Quality Assurance/Quality Control

The Company maintains geological logging, core photography and drill-record procedures for its Phase 2 drilling program at Majuba Hill. Mineral identifications reported for drill hole MHB-41 are based on preliminary visual field observations and geological interpretations. These observations do not establish metal grades, mineralized widths or economic significance and should not be considered a substitute for laboratory assay results.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Larry Segerstrom, M.Sc. (Geology), CPG, a non-independent consulting geologist to the Company and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

About Copper One Resources Corp.

Copper One Resources Corp. is focused on identifying, acquiring and advancing high-potential copper, copper-silver-gold and copper-molybdenum projects to help meet global demand for critical metals used in electrification, AI infrastructure and data centres, renewable energy, defence and power system modernization.

The Company's flagship asset is the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold District, located approximately 156 miles (251 kilometres) from Reno, Nevada. Majuba Hill is an exploration-stage porphyry copper project situated in an established mining jurisdiction with existing infrastructure, where ongoing exploration is focused on evaluating the scale and continuity of a copper-silver-gold mineralized system.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project, located northeast of Campbell River in British Columbia's Vancouver Mining Division. The district-scale project comprises approximately 2,746.46 hectares (6,786 acres) across nine mineral claims and hosts a porphyry-style copper-molybdenum system within the Coast Suture Zone, a geological belt known for porphyry copper and skarn mineralization. Systematic exploration is continuing to evaluate the scale and continuity of the mineralized system.

In addition, Copper One holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in the Redhill Property, located south of Ashcroft, British Columbia, adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway. The 4,736-hectare (11,704-acre) property hosts volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) mineralization prospective for copper, zinc, silver and gold, while also demonstrating potential for epithermal gold mineralization.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Sport Project in Utah through its wholly owned subsidiary, Rooinek Mining Corp., expanding the Company’s portfolio of North American copper exploration assets.

Copper One is advancing its portfolio through systematic exploration, modern geological modelling and disciplined technical evaluation. The Company remains committed to responsible exploration practices, technical transparency and the disciplined advancement of critical-metals projects across North America.

Varennes, Quebec, November 13, 2026 – TheNewswire - CHARBONE CORPORATION (TSXV: CH; OTCQB: CHHYF; FSE: K47) (“CHARBONE” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated industrial gases company focused on production, distribution and storage of clean ultra-high purity (“UHP”) hydrogen and other strategic industrial gases, today announces the filing of its 2025 Amended Consolidated Financial Statements and Management’s Discussion & Analysis, as well as the corresponding officers’ certificates, in connection with a routine continuous disclosure review conducted by staff at the Autorité des marchés financiers (“AMF”). The correction does not have any impact on operating loss nor the Company’s cash flows.

 

During the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, the Company agreed with certain suppliers to settle trade payables through the issuance of units. Each unit represented either one common share of the Company or one common share and one warrant of the Company. During the third quarter of 2026, following a review of the accounting treatment applied to these transactions, the Company concluded that certain gains on settlement of accounts payable had been incorrectly measured. The error of accounting entry has been corrected by restating the amounts recognized for the year ended December 31, 2025 to reflect the measurement of the equity instruments incorporating quoted prices in active market at the date the securities were issued and not at the time and conditions the Company concluded these transactions with some suppliers.

 

AMENDED 2025 IMPACTS:

  • Share capital and warrants amounts increased respectively by $1 million and $0.7 million with a net impact of nil on shareholder equity. 

  • No impact on total assets nor total liabilities. 

  • For the year ending December 31, 2025, the financial expense has increased by $1.7 million without any impact on operating loss nor the Company’s cash flows. 

“The correction is primarily linked to the appreciation of the share price between the negotiation of the suppliers’ settlement agreement occurred in 2025 and the issuance of the shares and management understands and agrees with the highly technical accounting treatment point of view articulated by the AMF,” said Benoit Veilleux, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary of CHARBONE. “CHARBONE will continue to take the regulator’s comments very seriously and has demonstrated its good faith throughout its discussions with staff members to explain the basis for its financial reporting.” 

The Company has provided corrective disclosure in the amended annual filings to address the matters described above. The Company is also continuously enhancing its disclosure controls and procedures, including its processes for preparing and reviewing financial reporting.

TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / Grid Metals Corp. (TSXV:GRDM)(OTCQB:MSMGF) ("Grid" or the "Company") has filed on SEDAR+ the independent technical report (the "Report") supporting the Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") for its 85%-owned Falcon West Cesium Property ("Falcon West" or the "Property") located in southeastern Manitoba, Canada. The MRE has an effective date of September 25, 2026, and was prepared in accordance with the Canadian Securities Administrators' National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101"). There are no material differences in the Report from the results disclosed in the Company's news release dated September 30, 2026. The Report is titled "Technical Report on the Mineral Resource Estimate for the Lucy South Cesium Deposit, Falcon West Project, Municipality of Reynolds, Manitoba, Canada" and was prepared by SGS Canada Inc. The Report can be found under the Company's issuer profile on SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.com).

Investors Relations Agreement with Peterson Capital

In addition to the consulting fees outlined to Peterson Capital in Grid's September 8, 2026 press release, Peterson Capital also received a C$5,000 expense deposit to cover anticipated marketing expenses associated with its investor outreach activities. The deposit is separate from the consulting fees disclosed in the aforementioned press release and is subject to reconciliation against actual expenses incurred.

About Cesium and the Cesium Market

Cesium is the heaviest stable alkali metal with a unique set of characteristics due to its position on the periodic table. It is highly reactive, has excellent photoelectric properties, and has a large ionic radius. It is the metal of choice across a number of applications, including atomic clocks, 5G infrastructure, defence targeting optics, and next-generation green tech.

Cesium is defined as a critical metal by both Canada and the U.S owing to its supply chain vulnerability. There is currently believed to be a significant shortage of cesium feedstock globally1. The industry revolves around extreme supply concentration with the United States and several European allies being 100% net import reliant for their cesium needs1. Pollucite has historically been the mineral of choice for cesium extraction given its high cesium content.

About Lucy South

  • The Lucy South cesium deposit contains an open pit measured resource for the Lithium-Cesium-Tantalum ("LCT") Zone of 51,500 tonnes at 2.58% Cs2O and 1.47% Li2O2; the LCT Zone encloses a higher-grade cesium-rich Pollucite Zone containing a measured resource of 15,600 tonnes at 5.19% Cs2O and 1.76% Li2O.
    • Total contained metal in the measured category of 1,322 tonnes Cs2O.
  • This resource is believed to be the second largest cesium resource in active development in the western world3.
  • The resource is contained within a highly-fractionated LCT pegmatite, the Lucy South pegmatite, and covers an area of ~120 metres by ~50 metres and has an average depth from surface of ~20 metres.
  • It is located 130 km east of Winnipeg and 500 metres north of the TransCanada Highway. It is proximal to the intra-continental railway system and Manitoba's low-cost hydro-electric power grid.
  • The resource is partly open along strike and down dip.

About Falcon West

  • The focus of the Falcon West joint venture between Grid (85%) and Avenir (15%) is to establish a producing cesium operation at the Lucy South cesium zone. Cesium is a rare critical metal with a number of forward-facing industrial uses. The scope of the project is to establish a small footprint operation that uses crushing and XRT ore sorting (no water utilized or extensive infrastructure) in the production of a cesium-bearing pollucite concentrate to be sold to downstream cesium chemical producers.
  • Falcon West consists of 124 unpatented mining claims located 130 km east of Winnipeg and is transected by the Trans Canada Highway. Most of Grid's exploration efforts have focused on the Lucy claims in the northeastern part of the property.
  • Exploration potential in the project area remains high with a number of occurrences of spodumene and pollucite mineralization noted in the immediate project area (the Artdon-Lucy target area) that extends for >1 km along strike and >500 metres across strike. Of note is a large gap in historical drilling between the Artdon LCT pegmatite occurrence in the west and the Lucy South and Lucy North LCT pegmatites in the east.
  • The Company is also eying the potential for outlining additional cesium resources in the project area. Drilling is expected to commence in January 2027 focused on expansion of the Lucy South resource and identifying new LCT pegmatites with cesium potential. A strong magnetic low anomaly interpreted to reflect a large volume of near surface granitic pegmatite coincides with the Artdon-Lucy pegmatite trend and extends several km along strike in both directions.

Quality Assurance and Quality Control

The Company's ongoing exploration program at the Falcon West cesium/lithium property is being supervised by Dave Peck, P.Geo. Grid Metals applies best practice quality assurance and quality control ("QAQC") protocols on all of its exploration programs. For the current program, all core was logged and sampled at the Company's core facility located on its Makwa nickel property. Generally, 1.0 metre sample lengths were used. Samples were bagged and tagged and then transported by secure carrier to the Activation Laboratories facility in Ancaster, Ontario for sample preparation and analysis for lithium, cesium, rubidium, tantalum and selected major and trace element abundances using a sodium peroxide fusion total digestion method followed by ICP-OES and ICP-MS analysis. The Company is using two rare metal certified reference materials ("CRMs") and an analytical blank for the program to monitor analytical accuracy and check for cross contamination between samples. The blank and CRM results for the reported intervals were determined to fall within the accepted range of deviation from the certified values. A check assay program using a similar sodium peroxide fusion digestion method has recently been initiated with check samples being analyzed at AGAT Laboratories in Thunder Bay, Ontario.

Qualified Person Statement

The Mineral Resource Estimate (MRE) was prepared by Rohan Millar, P.Geo., of SGS Geological Services in accordance with the 2014 Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum Definition Standards and Canadian National Instrument 43-101 ("NI 43-101"). Mr. Millar is an independent Qualified Person as defined by NI 43-101 and has reviewed and approved the contents of this news release.

Dr. Dave Peck, P.Geo., is a Qualified Person as defined in National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects ("NI 43-101") and has reviewed and approved the scientific and technical information disclosed in this release. Dr. Peck is not independent of the Company within the meaning of NI 43-101 as he is an officer of Grid.

About Grid Metals Corp.

The Company is one of the largest mineral rights holders in the Province of Manitoba with over 250,000 hectares of mineral claims and exploration licenses registered to Grid. The current focus of Grid is its Falcon West Property which is advancing towards commercial production following the release of a maiden cesium resource at the Lucy South deposit. A summary of Grid's mineral properties in Manitoba include:

  1. The Falcon West Property (Li-Cs) is located 130 km east of Winnipeg along the Trans-Canada highway and contains an open pit measured mineral resource at the Lucy South deposit of 51,500 tonnes grading 2.58% Cs2O and 1.47% Li2O2. The property is subject to a joint venture agreement with Avenir, which has a 15% interest in the property.
  2. The Makwa Property (Ni-Cu-PGM-Co), which is subject to an Option and Joint Venture Agreement with Teck Resources Limited ("Teck"). Teck can earn up to a 70% interest in Makwa by incurring a total of C$17.3 million, comprising project expenditures (C$15.7 million) and cash payments or equity participation (C$1.6 million) with Grid. Makwa is located on the south arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt and contains an open pit indicated mineral resource of 14.2 million tonnes grading 0.48% nickel, 0.11% copper, and 0.37 g/t palladium4.
  3. The Mayville Property (Cu-Ni) is located on the north arm of the Bird River Greenstone Belt. Grid owns a cumulative 89% interest in the project. The project contains an open pit indicated mineral resource of 32.0 million tonnes grading 0.40% copper, 0.16% nickel, and 0.13 g/t palladium4.
  4. The Donner Property (Li-Cs) is adjacent to the Mayville Property, and Grid owns 75% of the project. The project contains an open pit inferred mineral resource of 2.1 million tonnes grading 1.42% Li2O and an underground inferred mineral resource of 4.7 million tonnes grading 1.37% Li2O5.
  5. The Thompson East (Cu-Ni-PGM) Property is located east of the city of Thompson in north-central Manitoba and captures a number of high tenor Cu- and PGE-rich magmatic sulphide occurrences that are interpreted to be related to the development of the adjacent Thompson Nickel Belt. The property is subject to an Option and Joint Venture Agreement with Boliden Mineral Canada Ltd ("Boliden"). Boliden is currently sole-funding early-stage exploration on the property.
  6. The 100%-owned Fox River (Cu-Ni-PGM-Au) Property located in the Gillam region of northeastern Manitoba and covering 90 km of strike of the highly prospective Fox River Belt - a direct analogue to the Raglan nickel district in northern Quebec.

All of the Company's southeastern Manitoba projects are located on the ancestral lands of the Sagkeeng First Nation with whom the Company maintains an Exploration Agreement.

  1. US Geological Survey Mineral Commodity Summaries - Cesium - February 2026.
  2. NI 43-101 report by SGS Canada dated September 25, 2026 and entitled ‘Technical Report on the Mineral Resource Estimate for the Lucy South Cesium Deposit, Falcon West Project, Municipality of Reynolds, Manitoba, Canada.
  3. Power Metals Corp and PMET Resources are actively developing pollucite-bearing cesium projects. –First Quarter Revenue Increased 27% Year-over-Year to $5.4 Million; Revenue Plus Interest Income of $5.9 Million*–

–Stock Locate Revenue of $3.0 Million–

–Revenue from Sources Other Than Commissions Rose to 68% of Total Revenue, from 45%–

–AtlasClearing Net Capital Increased to $15.2 Million, $14.9 Million in Excess of Requirements–

–Definitive Agreement to Acquire Ark Financial Services Signed and FINRA Continuing Membership Application Filed; Correspondent Network Expanded to Nine Signed Agreements–

–Earnings Conference Call Scheduled for Monday, November 16, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET–

TAMPA, Fla., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AtlasClear Holdings, Inc. (“AtlasClear” or the “Company”) (ATCH), a company building regulated financial infrastructure for smaller institutions, fintechs and advisors, today announced financial results for its fiscal first quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Highlights

(Quarter Ended September 30, 2026)

  • Revenue increased 27% year-over-year to $5.4 million, compared to $4.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
  • Revenue plus interest income increased 24% to $5.9 million, compared to $4.7 million in the prior-year quarter.*
  • Revenue from sources other than commissions represented approximately 68% of total revenue, compared to approximately 45% in the prior-year quarter, reflecting continued diversification of the revenue base.
  • AtlasClearing’s net capital increased to $15.2 million at September 30, 2026, from $14.4 million at June 30, 2026, and was $14.9 million in excess of its minimum requirement, well above the $10 million excess net capital threshold the National Securities Clearing Corporation requires of firms that clear for introducing brokers.
  • Stockholders’ equity was $20.7 million at September 30, 2026.
  • Cash and cash equivalents totaled $9.4 million; total cash including segregated customer and PAB reserve cash totaled approximately $35.8 million.
  • Net loss was $1.1 million, or $(0.01) per share, compared to a net loss of $0.4 million, or $(0.01) per share, in the prior-year quarter. Operating expenses included approximately $1.3 million in regulatory, legal and professional fees, driven by the planned Ark Financial Services and Commercial Bancorp transactions, and $0.6 million in non-cash stock-based compensation.

*This is a non-GAAP financial measure; see below for additional information.

  • Compensation, payroll taxes and benefits expense declined 13% year-over-year to $2.7 million, while revenue grew 27%.

Management Commentary

“We are building exactly the business we set out to build, and this quarter shows it,” said John Schaible, Executive Chairman of AtlasClear Holdings. “Revenue grew 27%, we built stock locate into our largest revenue line, and AtlasClearing’s net capital rose to $15.2 million. And we grew revenue while compensation costs fell 13%, which tells us that not every new dollar of revenue requires more people. We delivered that growth before our newly signed correspondents made any material contribution, which gives us confidence in the opportunity ahead. I know the recent trading suspension has been difficult for our shareholders, and we take that seriously. The Exchange’s action is about our share price. It is not about AtlasClearing’s regulatory capital, the Company’s financial condition or our operations. We intend to pursue the appeal process and seek to restore trading on the NYSE American, and we intend to seek to effect a reverse stock split as part of our plan to support the appeal and our continued listing. But the share price is not the business. The business is growing, the team is executing, and nothing about our foundation has changed.”

“Stock locate is the clearest proof of what this platform can do,” said Craig Ridenhour, President of AtlasClear Holdings and Chairman of AtlasClearing, Inc. “A year ago it did not exist, and this quarter it generated $3.0 million, more than any other part of our business. That is what happens when you add a new service to infrastructure that is already built and well capitalized. Now we are doing the same thing with correspondents. Every firm we bring through onboarding adds accounts and trading activity to an engine that already earns revenue across commissions, clearing, stock locate and interest, and we expect to support much of that growth with the platform and team already in place. My team is in that work every day, and none of it has slowed down.”

Operational and Strategic Highlights

During and following the quarter, AtlasClear continued executing on its strategy to build an integrated financial services platform combining clearing, capital markets and banking capabilities. Key developments included:

  • In October 2026, signed a definitive business combination agreement to acquire Ark Financial Services, Inc., the parent of Dawson James Securities, Inc., and completed an initial 24.9% investment funded with $2.5 million in cash and a $2.5 million seller note, with no AtlasClear shares issued. Dawson James, an active underwriter and placement agent that already clears through AtlasClearing, reported 2025 revenue of $25.1 million and audited net income of $2.4 million. Because Ark’s principal serves on the Company’s board of directors, the transaction was reviewed and approved by AtlasClear’s independent directors.
  • On November 12, 2026, the continuing membership application for Dawson James was filed with FINRA. FINRA approval is the principal regulatory condition to the acquisition of the remaining 75.1% of Ark, which also remains subject to stockholder approval to the extent required and other customary closing conditions. The remaining consideration will be paid solely in cash and AtlasClear common stock, with no warrants, preferred stock, convertible securities, discounts or price resets, and Ark stockholders receiving AtlasClear shares will be subject to a six-month lock-up.
  • Expanded AtlasClearing’s correspondent network to nine signed correspondent broker-dealer agreements, four of which were signed since the start of fiscal 2027, with onboarding and conversion under way.
  • Continued to scale stock locate operations, which generated $3.0 million in revenue in the quarter, close to half of the $6.8 million generated in all of fiscal 2026, its first year of operation.
  • Remained committed to the planned acquisition of Commercial Bancorp of Wyoming, parent of Farmers State Bank, and expects to refile its regulatory applications at an appropriate time. The institutional digital asset opportunity announced in July 2026 remains subject to a non-binding letter of intent, due diligence and definitive agreements.

NYSE American Listing Update

On November 10, 2026, the Company announced that NYSE American had suspended trading in its common stock and commenced proceedings to delist the common stock, citing Section 1003(f)(v) of the NYSE American Company Guide based on the low selling price of the common stock. The Exchange’s determination is based solely on the low selling price of the common stock and does not relate to AtlasClearing’s regulatory capital compliance, the Company’s financial condition or the status of its correspondent clearing operations.

The Company intends to appeal the determination by requesting a hearing before a Listing Qualifications Panel of the Committee for Review of the Board of Directors of the Exchange, and currently intends to seek to effect a reverse stock split as part of its plan to support the appeal and its continued listing. During the appeal process, the common stock is being quoted on the OTC market under the symbol “ATCH.” AtlasClearing’s clearing operations continue in the ordinary course, and AtlasClearing remains compliant with its regulatory net capital requirements.

Fiscal First Quarter 2027 Financial Results

Revenue. Total revenue for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 was $5.4 million, an increase of 27% from $4.3 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by $3.0 million of stock locate fees, compared with none in the prior-year quarter. Revenue from sources other than commissions represented approximately 68% of total revenue, compared with approximately 45% in the prior-year quarter. Additional detail on revenue by line and on operating results will be available in the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Expenses and operating results. Total expenses were $7.9 million, compared with $5.1 million in the prior-year quarter. Compensation, payroll taxes and benefits declined 13% to $2.7 million from $3.1 million. Data processing and clearing costs increased to $1.9 million from $0.6 million, primarily reflecting costs associated with the stock locate business. Regulatory, professional and related expenses increased to $1.3 million from $0.3 million, driven by legal and professional advisory work on the planned Commercial Bancorp and Ark transactions. Non-cash stock-based compensation was $0.6 million, compared with $0.2 million. Loss from operations was $2.5 million, compared with $0.9 million in the prior-year quarter.

Other income and net loss. Total other income was $1.2 million, compared with $0.3 million in the prior-year quarter. The principal items included interest income of $0.5 million and non-cash gains of $0.7 million from the change in fair value of a secured convertible note, $0.3 million from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities and $0.2 million from the change in fair value of earnout liability, partially offset by interest expense of $0.4 million, a 72% decrease from $1.4 million in the prior-year quarter. After an income tax benefit of $0.2 million, net loss was $1.1 million, or $(0.01) per basic and diluted share, compared with a net loss of $0.4 million, or $(0.01) per share, in the prior-year quarter.

Balance Sheet and Capital

Total assets were $69.8 million at September 30, 2026. Stockholders’ equity was $20.7 million, compared to $21.1 million at June 30, 2026. AtlasClearing’s net capital increased $0.8 million during the quarter to $15.2 million. The change in cash and cash equivalents during the quarter primarily reflected net cash used in operating activities of $3.9 million, which included a $5.6 million increase in receivables from customers. AtlasClearing’s $10 million revolving line of credit with BMO Bank remained undrawn at September 30, 2026. Following the quarter, the Company paid $2.5 million in cash in connection with its initial investment in Ark, and it expects additional cash commitments of approximately $2.44 million payable at the closing of the Ark acquisition and $2.5 million under the seller note, which matures in January 2027 unless repaid earlier. Management’s base cash flow forecast indicates that projected operating cash flows and existing cash may not be sufficient to satisfy all anticipated obligations over the next twelve months. The Company is pursuing a committed PIPE financing, together with other available capital resources, to fund any potential shortfall, and based on these plans, management concluded that there is no substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.

Non-GAAP Financial Measure

Revenue plus interest income is a supplemental measure that is not calculated in accordance with GAAP. AtlasClear presents interest income, which is earned on balances held at its broker-dealer subsidiary, in other income. Management believes that adding interest income to total revenues provides a useful view of the revenue generated by the Company’s operations. This measure should not be considered a substitute for total revenues determined in accordance with GAAP.

Reconciliation: First quarter fiscal 2027 GAAP total revenue of $5.4 million plus interest income of $0.5 million equals total revenue plus interest income of $5.9 million. First quarter fiscal 2026 GAAP total revenue of $4.3 million plus interest income of $0.5 million equals total revenue plus interest income of $4.7 million.

About AtlasClear Holdings, Inc.

AtlasClear Holdings, Inc. is building a technology-enabled financial services platform designed for trading, clearing, settlement, and banking for emerging financial institutions and fintechs. Through its wholly owned subsidiary AtlasClearing, Inc. (formerly Wilson-Davis & Co., Inc.), a full-service correspondent broker-dealer registered with the SEC and FINRA, its pending acquisition of Ark Financial Services, Inc., and its planned acquisition of Commercial Bancorp of Wyoming, AtlasClear Holdings seeks to deliver a vertically integrated suite of investment banking, brokerage, clearing, risk management, regulatory, and commercial banking solutions.
