Edmonton, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 13, 2026) - Bri-Chem Corp. (TSX: BRY) ("Bri-Chem" or "Company"), a leading North American oilfield chemical distribution and blending company, is pleased to announce the appointment of Tony Pagnucco as Chief Operating Officer, effective immediately.

In his expanded role, Mr. Pagnucco will assume responsibility for all day-to-day operations across the Company's Canadian and U.S. businesses, including sales, operations and financial management. He will also continue overseeing the accounting, financial reporting and related responsibilities he has held as Chief Financial Officer since October 2020.

Barry Hugghins will remain President and CEO and Board Chairman, continuing to lead the Company's overall strategic direction, key business relationships and long-term priorities.

The appointment is part of Bri-Chem's ongoing efforts to strengthen operating performance, improve profitability and increase sustainable cash flow. The expanded leadership structure is intended to provide greater accountability for day-to-day execution while allowing Mr. Hugghins to focus on the Company's broader strategic objectives.

"Tony knows this company, its people and its challenges exceptionally well," said Barry Hugghins, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman. "Over the past six years, he has provided steady leadership and financial discipline through some difficult industry conditions. We believe putting our operations under his leadership will improve accountability, strengthen execution and help us build a more profitable business. I'll continue working closely with Tony as we focus on improving performance and positioning Bri-Chem for the future."

Mr. Pagnucco is a Chartered Professional Accountant with extensive experience in financial management and organizational leadership. Before joining Bri-Chem, he held leadership positions in manufacturing, real estate and heavy equipment servicing, following the start of his career at Deloitte.

"I appreciate the confidence Barry and the Board have placed in me," said Mr. Pagnucco. "Our focus is on improving how we operate, strengthening our sales efforts, improving margins and generating consistent cash flow. We have experienced people and longstanding customer relationships to build upon. My responsibility is to bring greater focus and accountability to daily operations and deliver measurable performance improvements."

Bri-Chem has established itself, through a combination of strategic acquisitions and organic growth, as the North American industry leader for wholesale distribution and blending of oilfield drilling, completion, stimulation and production chemical fluids. For investors, this shifts much of the expense and risk onto the tenant, creating a steadier, more predictable income stream for the property owner—similar to renting a furnished home where the renter also pays the bills—making valuation and cash-flow forecasting simpler.
reitfinancial
A real estate investment trust (REIT) is a company that owns, operates, or finances income-producing real estate, like shopping centers, apartments, or office buildings. For investors, REITs offer a way to invest in real estate without having to buy property directly, often providing regular income through dividends. They function like a mutual fund for real estate, making it easier for people to add property investments to their portfolio.
ebitdafinancial
EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. It measures a company's profitability by focusing on the money it makes from its core operations, ignoring expenses like taxes and accounting adjustments. Investors use EBITDA to compare how well different companies are performing financially, as it provides a clearer picture of operational success without the influence of financial structure or accounting choices.
View in glossary
adjusted ebitdafinancial
Adjusted EBITDA is a way companies measure how much money they make from their core operations, like running a business, by removing certain costs or income that aren’t part of regular business activities. It helps investors see how well a company is doing without distractions from unusual expenses or gains, making it easier to compare companies or track performance over time.

BRISBANE, Calif., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tempest Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: TPST) (“Tempest”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of advanced in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (“CAR-T”) product candidates to treat cancer and autoimmune disease, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update.

“The third quarter marked a period of meaningful progress in the advancement of two next-generation in vivo CAR-T platforms with the potential to transform treatment across multiple diseases,” said Matt Angel, Ph.D., president and chief executive officer of Tempest. “We made important strides in expanding our pipeline and strengthening our position in the rapidly evolving in vivo CAR-T landscape through our strategic collaboration with Senlang by obtaining exclusive license rights to our clinical-stage BCMA/GPRC5D in vivo CAR-T candidate TPST-4903, while securing access to additional capital to support our development priorities. We also welcomed two accomplished independent directors to our Board, bringing valuable corporate governance and capital markets expertise as we navigate our next phase of growth. Together, these achievements reinforce our commitment to advancing our pipeline, executing on our strategic priorities and unlocking the broad therapeutic potential of in vivo CAR-T therapies for patients.”

Recent Highlights

  • TPST-4903
    • Exercised option under agreement with Hebei Senlang Biotechnology Co., Ltd. to obtain an exclusive license to develop and commercialize Senlang’s CD7-targeted lentiviral vector platform and associated in vivo CAR-T candidates worldwide, excluding China.
    • The lead program, TPST-4903, is a BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeting in vivo CAR-T candidate being evaluated in a Phase 1 dose-escalation study in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (rrMM). The initial data demonstrating encouraging preliminary clinical responses are expected to be presented at an upcoming scientific conference.

  • TPST-4003

    • Unveiled next-generation in vivo CAR-T pipeline, including lead product candidate TPST-4003, a dual-targeting CD19/BCMA in vivo CAR-T candidate that combines the Company’s proprietary CD7-targeted mRNA/LNP delivery with its clinically validated dual-target CAR architecture for broad B-cell lineage depletion and reset.
    • Executed a strategic partnership in July 2026 with Hebei Senlang Biotechnology to collaborate on the development of certain of Tempest’s proprietary in vivo CAR-T product candidates, including the Company’s next-generation CD7-targeted TPST-4003. An investigator-initiated trial in China evaluating TPST-4003 in approximately 10 patients with myasthenia gravis or multiple sclerosis is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

  • Corporate:

    • Completed a private placement in September 2026 of pre-funded warrants and Series C and D warrants for gross proceeds of approximately $2.5 million (approximately $1.8 million net of placement agent fees and offering expenses), excluding up to approximately $5.0 million of gross proceeds that may be received upon the cash exercise of the Series C and D warrants.
    • Entered into a purchase agreement with Lincoln Park Capital Fund, LLC on August 13, 2026 that gives Tempest the right, but not the obligation, to sell up to $25.0 million of its common stock, increasing to $50.0 million if the initial amount is sold, over a 24-month period that began September 1, 2026.Through September 30, 2026, Tempest sold 350,000 shares to Lincoln Park for gross proceeds of approximately $0.3 million.
    • Strengthened Board of Directors with the appointments of independent directors, Nancy Freda-Smith and John W. Frederick boosting corporate governance and capital markets expertise.

Financial Results

Third Quarter 2026

  • Tempest ended the quarter with $0.9 million in cash and cash equivalents, compared to $7.7 million on December 31, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to cash used in operations, including one-time transaction-associated costs incurred prior to or upon closing of the Asset Acquisition in February 2026, offset by the net proceeds from the Company’s private placement of common stock and warrants in March 2026 of $1.7 million, the warrant inducement in May 2026 of $1.7 million, sales of common stock under the Lincoln Park equity line of credit of $0.3 million and the Company’s private placement in September 2026 of $1.8 million. The Company’s existing cash and cash equivalents are expected to fund its projected operating expense requirements for less than 12 months from the date the financial statements were available to be issued, and there is substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
  • Net loss and net loss per share for the quarter were $3.6 million and $0.21, respectively, compared to $3.5 million and $0.79, respectively, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Research and development expenses for the quarter were $0.2 million compared to $0.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $0.4 million decrease was primarily due to a decrease in costs incurred as a result of the portfolio re-prioritization after the Asset Acquisition in February 2026, offset by research and manufacturing costs related to the Company’s CAR-T product candidates.
  • General and administrative expenses for the quarter were $2.6 million compared to $3.0 million for the same period in 2025. The $0.4 million decrease was primarily due to a decrease in one-time separation and other costs incurred in the third quarter of 2025, offset by other administrative expenses.
  • Financing costs related to the Lincoln Park equity line of credit for the quarter were $0.8 million, consisting of $0.66 million for the fair value of the commitment shares issued to Lincoln Park and $0.15 million of issuance costs, net of a nominal gain on shares sold to Lincoln Park. There were no financing costs in the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026

  • Cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $12.4 million.
  • Net loss and net loss per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $36.6 million and $2.54, respectively, compared to $22.2 million and $5.71, respectively, for the same period in 2025.
  • Research and development expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $2.1 million, compared to $12.1 million for the same period in 2025. The $9.9 million decrease was primarily due to a decrease in costs incurred as a result of re-prioritizing efforts towards exploring strategic alternatives initiated in April 2025 and resulting in the Asset Acquisition completed in February 2026.
  • General and administrative expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $11.5 million, compared to $10.4 million for the same period in 2025. The $1.0 million increase was primarily due to one-time costs resulting from the Asset Acquisition completed in February 2026.
  • Acquired in-process research and development expenses for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $22.2 million compared to nil for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Costs incurred prior to or upon closing the Asset Acquisition in the prior three months ended March 31, 2026 were expensed as acquired in-process research and development.
  • Financing costs related to the Lincoln Park equity line of credit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 were $0.8 million, all of which were recognized in the third quarter of 2026. There were no financing costs in the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

About Tempest Therapeutics

Tempest is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a pipeline of advanced in vivo CAR-T therapies designed to treat cancer and autoimmune disease by resetting dysfunctional immunity. Tempest’s portfolio includes TPST-4903, a BCMA/GPRC5D dual-targeting in vivo CAR-T candidate being evaluated in a Phase 1 study for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (rrMM). The Company’s lead lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based in vivo CAR-T candidate, TPST-4003 combines a clinically supported dual-targeting CD19/BCMA CAR structure with an advanced CD7-targeting delivery platform to support broad immune reset across multiple indications. The company’s additional preclinical programs leverage advanced payloads to create a modular in vivo CAR-T portfolio. Tempest envisions a world in which immune reset therapies bring safe, effective, and broadly accessible therapeutic options to patients in need. Key Terms

long-term capital gainsfinancial
Profit realized when an investor sells an asset they have owned longer than the legally specified holding period; these gains are taxed under “long-term” rules that typically carry lower tax rates than gains on assets sold quickly. It matters to investors because lower tax rates increase the amount of money they keep after a sale, so holding an investment longer can be like letting a high-interest coupon compound before withdrawing the cash, affecting decisions about when to sell and overall portfolio returns.
View in glossary
qualified dividendsfinancial
Dividends that meet tax rules allowing them to be taxed at the lower long-term capital gains rates instead of higher ordinary income rates. For investors, that means more of the payment stays in your pocket; it influences which dividend-paying stocks you buy and how long you hold them, similar to getting a discount for meeting a store’s membership conditions.
closed-end investment companyfinancial
A closed-end investment company is a pooled investment fund that issues a fixed number of shares in a one-time offering and then has those shares bought and sold on an exchange like a stock; a professional manager runs the portfolio of assets. It matters to investors because the market price can move above or below the value of the underlying holdings, affecting returns and income, and shares may be less flexible to issue or redeem compared with open-ended funds—think of buying a slice of a privately baked pie whose market price can differ from the pie’s actual ingredients value.

Manufacturing Work Addressing FDA CMC Information Requests Substantially Completed

NDA Resubmission Expected Between December 2026 and January 2027

KANSAS CITY, Kan., Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cingulate Inc. (NASDAQ: CING), a biopharmaceutical company utilizing its proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) drug delivery platform to develop a pipeline of next-generation products, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and announced that it has substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) information requests for CTx-1301. The Company expects to resubmit the new drug application (NDA) for CTx-1301 between December 2026 and January 2027.

“With the manufacturing work substantially complete, we are now finalizing the data and documentation needed to resubmit the NDA for CTx-1301, and we expect to do so by January 2027, potentially sooner,” stated Cingulate Chairman and CEO Shane J. Schaffer. “Importantly, the FDA’s Complete Response Letter did not raise any concerns about the clinical safety or efficacy of CTx-1301. We thank our shareholders for their patience and continued support as we work to bring this treatment to patients with ADHD.”

Regulatory Update: CTx-1301 NDA Resubmission Progress

On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter (CRL) for the CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) NDA. The CRL identified specific requests for additional CMC information and did not identify any concerns regarding the clinical safety or efficacy of CTx-1301, the Company’s lead ADHD asset.

Since then, Cingulate and its contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO), Bend Bioscience, have substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests in the CRL and are finalizing the supporting data and documentation for resubmission. As announced on November 9, 2026, the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2027. After the FDA receives the resubmission, it is expected to classify it as a Class 1 or Class 2 resubmission, which carry review goals of two and six months, respectively.

Third Quarter Financial Results

Cash and Working Capital: As of September 30, 2026, Cingulate had approximately $23.2 million in cash and cash equivalents, compared to $11.0 million as of December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by capital raised during the first nine months of 2026, including the close of a $12.0 million private placement in the first quarter and $22.5 million of capital raised on Cingulate’s At-the-Market Agreement with AGP and Purchase Agreement with Lincoln Park Capital, partially offset by $20.4 million in cash used for operations. As of September 30, 2026, Cingulate had approximately $18.8 million in working capital, an increase of $16.1 million as compared to December 31, 2025.

Under its current business plan, the Company believes its cash and cash equivalents will be sufficient to fund operations into mid-2027, including costs associated with seeking regulatory approval for CTx-1301, and continuing the build-out of commercial readiness capabilities.

R&D Expenses: Research and development expenses were $2.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 2.2% from $2.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, driven primarily by higher drug manufacturing costs to address the CMC information requested in the FDA’s CRL, partially offset by lower clinical operations costs following the conclusion of clinical study activities in early 2025, the absence of regulatory costs incurred in the prior-year period in connection with preparing the CTx-1301 NDA, and lower personnel expenses. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, R&D expenses were $6.6 million, a decrease of 15.3% from $7.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, driven primarily by lower clinical operations and regulatory costs, partially offset by increased manufacturing activities related to CTx-1301 following the CRL.

SG&A Expenses: Selling, general and administrative expenses (SG&A) were $4.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 45.5%. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, SG&A expenses were $14.2 million, compared to $6.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 116.6%. The increases were driven primarily by the build-out of commercial readiness capabilities, including increased headcount and expanded market access, pricing, reimbursement and medical affairs activity conducted through Indegene, the Company’s commercialization partner.

Net Loss: Net loss was $7.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $7.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net loss was $22.9 million, compared to $16.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increases primarily reflect the higher SG&A expenses described above, partially offset in the third quarter by a smaller loss from the change in fair value of derivative and lower interest expense, and for the nine-month period by lower R&D expenses.

About Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

ADHD is a chronic neurobiological and developmental disorder that affects millions of children and often continues into adulthood. The estimated market size of the US ADHD market is approximately 100 million annual prescriptions. The condition is marked by an ongoing pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development. In the U.S., over 20 million patients have been diagnosed with ADHD. Among this group, 12 million are adults and over 8 million are under the age of 17. According to the CDC, just 53.6 percent of all children and teens with ADHD reported they were actively treating their symptoms with medication in 2022, with 65-90 percent demonstrating clinical ADHD symptoms that persist into adulthood. Current market trends demonstrate that adult ADHD prevalence is larger and growing faster than the child and adolescent segments combined.

About CTx-1301

CTx-1301 (dexmethylphenidate HCl) is a once-daily, multi-core tablet utilizing Cingulate’s proprietary Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) platform to deliver three precisely timed releases of active medication across the day. This design aims to provide rapid onset of effect and entire active-day duration. CTx-1301 is being evaluated for the treatment of ADHD under the FDA’s 505(b)(2) pathway. In October 2025, the FDA accepted for review the NDA for CTx-1301 and assigned a PDUFA target action date of May 31, 2026. On June 1, 2026, the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for the CTx-1301 NDA; the Company and its CDMO have since substantially completed the manufacturing work required to address the CMC requests, and the Company expects to resubmit the NDA between December 2026 and January 2026. There can be no assurance regarding the timing of any resubmission or whether approval will occur.

About Precision Timed Release™ (PTR™) Platform Technology

Cingulate is developing ADHD and anxiety disorder product candidates capable of achieving true once-daily dosing using Cingulate’s innovative PTR drug delivery platform technology. It incorporates a proprietary Erosion Barrier Layer (EBL) providing control of drug release at precise, pre-defined times with no release of drug prior to the intended release. The EBL technology is enrobed around a drug-containing core to give a tablet-in-tablet dose form. It is designed to erode at a controlled rate until eventually the drug is released from the core tablet. The EBL formulation, Oralogik™, is licensed from BDD Pharma. Cingulate intends to utilize its PTR technology to expand and augment its clinical-stage pipeline by identifying and developing additional product candidates in other therapeutic areas in addition to Anxiety and ADHD.
